acceptance.given: A Toolchain write operation is proposed against each protected Phase, runtime, Hosted workspace, account, and user-sandbox path category.

oracle.expected: Every attempted write is deterministically rejected, leaves the target unchanged, and reports a boundary violation; the same enforcement applies across all five protected categories.
forbidden: Any Phase, runtime, Hosted workspace, account, or user-sandbox file is modified under this scope.
oracle.observable: The boundary validator returns a rejection for each protected-path fixture and byte/state comparison confirms no protected file changed.

acceptance.then: The protected-path boundary check is evaluated before any filesystem mutation is permitted.
acceptance.when: The Toolchain boundary validator is executed against the protected-path fixtures.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Use the protected-path negative validator to demonstrate that a proposed write to a Phase, runtime, Hosted workspace, account, or user-sandbox path is accepted instead of rejected.
Use the protected-path negative validator to detect any protected target whose bytes or existence changed after the attempted write.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce a Toolchain-only, fail-closed write boundary: before filesystem mutation, classify repository-relative targets and reject all Phase, runtime, Hosted workspace, account, and user-sandbox paths while preserving protected-target bytes and state. The check must not authorize or modify Phase service or sandbox code.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Rollback removes only the boundary-enforcement change and preserves existing receipt, schema, and lifecycle semantics; no protected path or live database state is altered.

slice_hint.state_transition: proposed write -> protected-path classification -> deterministic rejection with no mutation
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: All five protected path categories produce rejection results and byte/state checks show no protected target changed; any accepted write or mutation is a failed terminal result.

acceptance.given: A Toolchain verdict is pending evaluation with its source identity and execution record available for inspection.

oracle.expected: The verdict is traceable to current source identity and real execution evidence, with no assistant prose serving as authoritative evidence.
forbidden: Assistant prose is used as the sole or authoritative basis for a verdict.
A verdict is accepted without source or execution evidence.
oracle.observable: The validation inspects the verdict artifact and its referenced current source identity and execution evidence during acceptance evaluation.

acceptance.then: The verdict is evidence-based and independent of assistant prose.
acceptance.when: The Toolchain acceptance selector evaluates whether a verdict may be accepted.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Evaluate a verdict lacking current source identity or real execution evidence and require acceptance validation to fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Require the Toolchain verdict artifact to bind current source identity and real execution evidence, excluding assistant prose as an evidentiary authority.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted state or schema change; revert removes only the Toolchain verdict-evidence enforcement.

slice_hint.state_transition: unevaluated verdict -> verdict accepted only with inspectable source and execution evidence
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Acceptance evaluation can inspect current source identity and real execution evidence for the verdict and rejects prose-only or evidence-free verdicts.

acceptance.given: An external process or aggregate reaches its configured time or output budget limit.

oracle.expected: The bounded execution reaches a deterministic unsuccessful terminal result.
forbidden: Budget exhaustion is classified as successful.
Budget exhaustion is treated as an indeterminate success or omitted outcome.
oracle.observable: A real budget-exhaustion execution is evaluated through the external-process and aggregate terminal-state path.

acceptance.then: The budget-exhausted execution has an unsuccessful terminal result.
acceptance.when: A configured execution budget is exhausted.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the authored S11 behavior selector with a process or aggregate that exhausts its configured time or output budget and observe the unsuccessful terminal outcome.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Classify a time- or output-budget-exhausted external process or aggregate as a deterministic unsuccessful terminal result.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Restore only Toolchain execution-result handling; no Phase service state or schema changes are permitted.

slice_hint.state_transition: An external process or aggregate reaches a time or output budget limit -> The budget-exhausted execution has an unsuccessful terminal result.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A budget-exhaustion run terminates deterministically as unsuccessful and is never published as successful, indeterminate success, or omitted.

acceptance.given: A detached negative Probe is configured to report success despite a false-negative condition.

oracle.expected: Acceptance evaluation classifies the always-success false-negative Probe as failed.
oracle.observable: The independent Probe evaluation reports a failed Probe outcome for the always-success false-negative condition.

acceptance.then: Always-success false negatives are reported as failures.
acceptance.when: The Toolchain Probe evaluator checks the detached negative Probe outcome.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Evaluate an always-success detached negative Probe and require the Probe-contract validation to fail if it is treated as passing.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce the detached-Probe contract so an always-success false negative is classified as a failed Probe outcome.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No persisted state or schema change; revert restores prior Toolchain Probe evaluation behavior.

slice_hint.state_transition: always-success false-negative Probe presented -> failed Probe outcome
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The evaluator emits a failed Probe outcome for an always-success false negative; it cannot be accepted as passing.
